tests.mutation: Players.Adversary returned the player himself (`player` for `player == Player.White ? Player.Black : Player.White`), so one person plays alone; this test went red. It went red too with Players.Both reduced to White alone, and with a third value, Red, added to Player.
Position.ToSlots refused only a side of more than fifteen (`total > MenPerPlayer` for `total != MenPerPlayer`); this test went red on fourteen.
Position.MenPerPlayer set to 14; this test went red.
Geometry.QuarterOf ended the inner table at pip 5 (`<= 5 => Quarter.OwnInner`); this test went red.
The same mutation, the inner table ending at pip 5; this test went red.
Geometry.NameOf called an outer table's first point the ace point rather than the bar point; this test went red.
Setup.Arrangement put the three men on pip 7 instead of pip 8; this test went red.
Opening.RollForTheRight gave the right to begin to the lower die; this test went red.
The same mutation, the lower die begins; this test went red.
Opening.RollForTheRight accepted the first pair thrown, ties included (`attempt.First > 0` for `attempt.First != attempt.Second`); this test went red.
Opening.OpeningThrow inverted the option (`!adopt ? roll.Deciding : Throw(source)`); this test went red.
The same mutation, the option inverted; this test went red.
Opening.Throw threw one die and doubled its face instead of throwing the pair; this test went red.
Movement.MovesForDie let only the rearmost man move, so the trois could not go to another man; this test went red.
Movement.MovesForDie offered a move past the ace point before bearing off (`to < 1 || IsPermittedDestination(...)` for `to >= 1 && IsPermittedDestination(...)`); this test went red.
Geometry.Mirror returned its argument, so both players' courses ran the same way; this test went red.
The same mutation, Mirror as the identity; this test went red.
Movement.Entitlement gave doublets two numbers instead of four; this test went red.
Movement.IsPermittedDestination refused a point holding one adversary man (`== 0` for `<= 1`); this test went red.
Position.HasMadePoint required three men (`>= 3` for `>= 2`); this test went red.

The same mutation, three men to a point; this test went red. Before it was strengthened it checked only the six point, which starts with five men, and stayed green; it now checks White's 24, which starts with exactly two.
Position.Apply removed a hit blot from its point without putting it on the bar; this test went red.
The same mutation, a hit blot not put on the bar; this test went red.
Movement.MovesForDie never took the entry branch, so a player with a man up moved his other men; this test went red.
The same mutation, the entry branch never taken; this test went red.
Movement.MustEnterFromBar held only for exactly one man up (`== 1` for `> 0`); this test went red.
The same mutation, exactly one man up; this test went red.
Movement.MovesForDie refused entry onto a point the entering player's own men hold -- the strict reading 0006 rejected; this test went red.
Movement.IsWhollySuspended always returned false; this test went red.
Movement.IsWhollySuspended counted a point as full on two men of either side -- the literal reading 0006 rejected; this test went red.

LegalPlays.For offered every partial play as well as the whole one (a terminal at every node, and no filter to the compelled use); this test went red. The maximal filter alone removed was not caught by it, because from the start every leaf is whole.
The same mutation, partial plays offered; this test went red.
LegalPlays.For declined only when more than two uses were maximal (`> 2` for `> 1`), silently playing the first; this test went red.
The same mutation, the incomparable case resolved silently; this test went red.

LegalPlays.For compelled only the higher number where the throw could not be played whole: when the one playable number was the lower, it returned the empty play instead; this test went red (the trois case). Before it was strengthened it tested only a playable six and stayed green. It also went red when any throw not playable whole was forfeited entirely. Removing the maximal-use filter cannot turn it red, and no test of this case could: where only one die is ever playable every unextendable line uses that die once, so the filter removes nothing.
BearingOff.IsEligible ignored a man on pip 7 (the outer-table loop started at 8); this test went red.
BearingOff.IsEligible ignored a single man on the bar (`> 1` for `> 0`); this test went red.
BearingOff.MovesForDie never removed a man from the point the die names; this test went red.
BearingOff.MovesForDie offered no forward move within the table; this test went red.
BearingOff.MovesForDie applied the modern rule, bearing off only from a point below the die; this test went red and no other did.
BearingOff.MovesForDie bore off from the lowest occupied point instead of the highest; this test went red.
LegalPlays refused to mix bearing off and moving within one doublets play (the 'or both' dropped); this test went red.
LegalPlays refused any bearing off with doublets; this test went red. It stayed green under the no-mixing mutation above.
BearingOff.HasWon required more than fifteen men off, so nobody ever won; this test went red.
BearingOff.HasWon held once any man was off; this test went red. The_last_man_off_wins_the_game stayed green under it.
Outcome.ValueOf called it a gammon while the loser had borne off two or fewer (`<= 2` for `== 0`); this test went red.
Outcome.ValueOf ignored a loser's man on the bar; this test went red.
Outcome.ValueOf called the uncovered finish a hit instead of declining; this test went red.
AgreedBackgammonMultiple admitted a multiple of 2 as well as 3 and 4; this test went red.
Outcome.Pays inferred thrice when no agreement was given, instead of throwing; this test went red.
Outcome.Pays paid a gammon the single stake; this test went red.
Outcome.Pays paid a backgammon thrice whatever was agreed; this test went red.
Outcome.Pays paid a hit double; this test went red.
Outcome.Pays paid a hit the agreed multiple less two, so it varied with the agreement; this test went red.
Outcome.Next inverted the hit test (`!=` for `==`); this test went red.
The same mutation, Next inverted; this test went red.
Game.Play rolled for the right to begin even when an opener was supplied; this test went red.
Die.D6 constructed a five-faced die; this test went red.
